name: Your face from the first frame
what: The hook is the speaker saying it, from frame 0; never an intro screen.
when: Every short. A voice line is a bridge in the middle, over a cutaway, never the opening.
why: Round 1 refused (« j'aime pas du tout les styles »); a voice line on the paper as the opening was refused.

name: Document Headline, Captions and Desk styles
what: The first three looks: the long video's Document look with a new type system, an intro screen for the hook.
when: Never. Dynamic text with the long video's pictures replaced them.
why: « j'aime pas du tout les styles ».

name: Dynamic text as the base
what: The words in the short editor's vertical language: Impact capitals, the payoff in yellow, one Sacramento accent, two-layer shadows, the glitch, the opening de-zoom, the SFX pack and its flash.
when: Every short, all along (the feed plays muted), verbatim.
why: « vraiment pas mal »; not a new type system.

name: Words in the room above the head, two lines at most
what: With the wider framing, the words sit above the head at y 0.135, behind it (the matte), the top of the room in shadow, two lines a screen at most.
when: Every short; over a cutaway the words come in front of it.
why: « normalement il met les sous-titres au-dessus de moi, un peu derrière moi »; a third line sank behind the head.

name: Never one or two words alone on a screen
what: A phrase is never split so that one or two words stand alone, and a phrase leaves before the next one lands.
when: Always.
why: A phrase cut at its 7th word left « things. » alone on a screen while the last one left.

name: Caption line on a white pill
what: The caption line uses the long video's white pill so it reads on any shirt.
when: Where a caption line is shown.
why: White captions on a white T-shirt were unreadable.

name: Wider reframe with the wall prolonged
what: A landscape take is sliced 1.25 times wider than 9:16, the speaker at the bottom, the wall prolonged above them (top rows stretched and softened, a 90 px fade).
when: Every landscape take; a vertical take is kept whole.
why: « on est très zoomé sur ma tête »; picked on stills among x1.0, x1.25, x1.45.

name: Blurred copy of the frame above the head
what: Filling the room above the head with a blurred copy of the frame.
when: Never; the wall is prolonged instead.
why: It showed a blurred head; refused before it was shown.

name: Three lengths of each subject
what: Each subject in about 30 s, 1 min and 1 min 30, the same hook, the longer ones explaining further with more of the take.
when: Every run, fewer when the take does not hold them.
why: « tu fais des extraits trop courts… j'ai même pas eu le temps d'expliquer mon propos ».

name: Reorganised, never rewritten
what: The user's real words in the order that makes the short, the strongest line moved first as the hook; retakes left out, pauses over 0.30 s cut with about 0.18 s of air kept.
when: Every short.

name: Cloned voice line as a bridge
what: Where a short needs a line the take does not have (a hook, a bridge), the user's clone says it in their words, 15 words at most, always under a cutaway.
when: One or two lines a short at most; never a fact, number, name or result they did not say.

name: Hook title above the head
what: The problem as a title above the head in the first 3 s, read first when someone scrolls, before the words begin.
when: The opening of every short.
why: Asked for a visual hook; Ihsane picked the title and it was kept in round 4.

name: Hook panel on the chest
what: A designed card on the chest with a yellow tag and the problem in Impact with the marker, one line.
when: An alternative to the hook title in the first 3 s.
why: Shown as one of the ways; the title was picked. Status of the panel not written in the docs.

name: Mood pictures from behind the head
what: Four to six pictures of the subject (Nano Banana 2 stickers, real tool icons) out from behind the head in two columns clear of the face, gone as the words begin.
when: The opening of every short, with the hook title.
why: « quelques petites images qui donnent le mood… en rapport avec le sujet ».

name: Behind you style
what: The pictures slide out from behind the head and shoulders; the screens and prints live behind the speaker.
when: The default style (needs the matte).
why: « la 5, c'est la meilleure ».

name: Prints style
what: The pictures pinned over the top of the frame: stock shots as floating screens, GIFs as pinned prints, on the chest under the words.
when: When the user picks it instead of the default.
why: Offered as one of three ways; Behind you was chosen as the default. Not refused in the docs.

name: Cutaways style
what: Stock shots over the whole frame for a beat or two with the screen effect and the flash on the cut; GIFs dropped on the face as big prints.
when: When the user picks it instead of the default.
why: Offered as one of three ways; Behind you was chosen as the default. Not refused in the docs.

name: Stock shot as a floating screen
what: A stock shot with rounded corners, a white rim, two shadows lifting while it flies, the screen grid, grain, vignette, a light sweep and a motion-blurred entrance.
when: On the words it illustrates; the style decides where it goes.
why: Asked for the long video's pictures with their effects.

name: GIF as a pinned print
what: A GIF with a white border, the yellow pin, two shadows and motion blur.
when: Sometimes, on the words it illustrates; organic use only.

name: Full-frame cutaway
what: A stock shot over the whole frame with the screen effect, a slow push and the pack's flash on the cut.
when: Always under a voice line; also in the Cutaways style.

name: Opening de-zoom, alternating jump cuts and punches
what: The de-zoom 1.30 to 1.00 with its whoosh, then the jump cuts alternating wide and close, and a punch on a payoff word.
when: Every short.

name: Something new every 3 to 6 s
what: Besides the words, a picture on its words (stock, GIF, logo, number, page) every 3 to 6 s, true only.
when: In every length, the long versions too.
why: « ça manque peut-être un peu de plans ».

name: Nothing on a page restates the voice
what: No editorial line saying what the speaker says and no caption under a GIF; the subtitles carry the words, the page carries a picture of them, only short labels.
when: Always.
why: « on met trop de texte à l'écran pour rien… je l'ai déjà dit à l'oral… le but c'est d'illustrer ».

name: White page
what: The long video's V-page move in white: a torn top edge rising in 0.45 s with motion blur and a warm light, leaving upwards by its torn bottom edge, to set an idea down.
when: 2 or 3 in a 1 min+ version, none in a 30 s one; it covers the frame before its first word.
why: Asked for more shots (round 5).

name: Simple page schemas: cards in a grid, balls in a funnel
what: The old simple pages: cards in a row or grid, balls falling into a funnel, a 16:9 schema cropped into a column, the knocked-out 95 %.
when: Never again; motion pages replaced them.
why: « pas fou… on peut faire 100 fois mieux »; a zoom cut their content top and bottom.

name: Number knocked out onto the face
what: A number counts in ink across the page width, then is knocked out so the face shows through the letters as the camera pushes in, and the page leaves through it.
when: Never in its round-9 form; the recap motion page replaced it.
why: Asked in round 7, then judged « pas fou » with the other round-9 pages in round 10.

name: Pages drawn by the long video's engine
what: A white page's content drawn by the long video's Document engine (method list, marker lines, profile cards, counters), cropped to fill the width.
when: Replaced by motion pages since round 10.
why: Asked in round 6, then the round-9 pages built this way were judged « pas fou » and cropped by the zoom.

name: Ways to make a page live
what: Round 8's six ways: the page as it was, the face in a window of the page, the camera's journey, collage and ink, a video in the page, a breathing page.
when: Never; the moving schema won over all of them.
why: The schema that moves won over all of them (round 9).

name: The idea as a moving schema
what: A page draws the reasoning (a hierarchy, a path, a filter, a flow, a before/after) as a schema animated on the words, the camera following the action, labels only.
when: Every white page; never cards in a row.
why: « là, c'est vraiment beaucoup mieux… très pédagogique, fais-moi pareil pour les autres ».

name: Motion page at After Effects level
what: A gsap scene over the whole vertical frame, rendered with alpha and laid on the sheet: depth, kinetic type, fast moves with overshoot and motion blur, things that transform into the next.
when: Every white page since round 10, varied from one short to the next; designer agents in parallel when available.
why: « j'aime énormément… les trois, faut les garder en référence ».

name: Motion page handoff onto the face
what: The last page takes the paper over and cuts it to open onto the face, with its own camera steps.
when: The page that exits onto the face.

name: Tree A: 3D floor
what: A decision tree as a 3D floor of photo cards, the camera riding a yellow road up.
when: A reference for a hierarchy page; do not repeat a concept in the next short.
why: Kept as a reference: « j'aime énormément » all three trees.

name: Tree B: type tree
what: A type-only decision tree, rank shown by font weight, ink branches, a highlighter climbing.
when: The chosen tree page.
why: Chosen in the round-10 review.

name: Tree C: elevator
what: The company as a tower, the frame an elevator with a rolling floor counter.
when: A reference for a hierarchy page.
why: Kept as a reference: « j'aime énormément » all three trees.

name: Radar A: job feed
what: A job feed at speed, posts lifted in 3D, a card flip to the team.
when: A reference for a signal page.
why: Kept among the nine references; not among the liked radars (B and C). Verdict not written.

name: Radar B: isometric city
what: An isometric city whose hiring buildings light up.
when: A reference for a signal page; its sound levels are right.
why: Liked in review; folded into radar D.

name: Radar C: signal wave
what: A field of company marks in depth crossed by one wave, a dive into a round table.
when: A reference for a signal page.
why: Liked in review, but its chart was « timide »; folded into radar D.

name: Radar D: city that transforms into the stage
what: B's city, then the platform itself transforms into C's round table (no floating island), then a full layered chart filling the bottom of the frame.
when: The chosen signal page.
why: Asked by Ihsane from B and C: « pas timide ».

name: Recap A: rows sliced by scanners
what: Rows sliced by scanners, the list becomes a band that peels into the payoff number, glyphs lift off, the paper leaves in strips.
when: A reference for a recap page.
why: Kept among the nine references; recap B was chosen. Verdict on A not written.

name: Recap B: odometer and blade split
what: 1000 dots filtered to 50, an odometer rolling to the number across the width, the % slash becomes a blade that splits the page into two doors onto the face.
when: The chosen recap page, the exit onto the face.
why: Chosen in the round-10 review.

name: Recap C: three rings into portholes
what: Three filter rings that become the counters of the number, punched out, a dive through one onto the eye.
when: A reference for a recap page.
why: Kept among the nine references; recap B was chosen. Verdict on C not written.

name: Motion page control
what: One move at a time, separate zones, a fixed depth order, hand-offs not crossfades, the whole frame used, only the frame's edge cuts an element; checked frame by frame.
when: Every motion page.

name: Motion page brand
what: Paper, ink #1A1A1A, yellow #FFD90D as the one accent, Bricolage at several weights, Geist Mono for small labels, soft blurred shadows, fictional people and companies; 3-6 pack cues at about -16 to -19.
when: Every motion page; subtitles band y 192-450 left empty, information inside x 103-977, y 450-1488.

name: End card A: CRT off
what: The screen turns off like a CRT, then a YouTube-like player powers on with the long video's thumbnail.
when: Kept as another way for the end card.
why: Card B was chosen; a and c kept as other ways.

name: End card B: phone on the paper desk
what: The screen turns off, the phone falls onto the paper desk and wakes on the thumbnail in a YouTube player with the channel row, a tilted YouTube logo, « Watch the entire video » and a cursor clicking play.
when: An option offered at the start of every run from a long video; the channel is Your brand's.
why: Chosen in round 12, with the channel shown under the player.

name: End card C: glitch into the scrubber
what: A glitch off, the dot becomes the scrubber and the bar the hinge the player swings up from.
when: Kept as another way for the end card.
why: Card B was chosen; a and c kept as other ways.

name: One calm music 19 LU under the voice
what: One calm track under the whole short, 19 LU under the voice, the figures' own sounds from the packs, nothing per word; -14 LUFS, true peak at most -1 dBTP.
when: Every short (the long video's track by default).
why: « La musique est peut-être un peu trop forte »: 15 LU was too loud; « un truc un peu moins commercial ».

name: The crickets GIF
what: A GIF of crickets used as a joke on silence.
when: Never in that short; removed in round 5.
why: « retire le GIF avec le cafard ».

name: Free commercial licences only
what: Stock from Pexels or Mixkit Free; Mixkit Restricted is refused; GIFs for organic use only, said at delivery.
when: Always.

name: Feed safe zones
what: Every figure clamps itself inside the feed's safe area; the sheet is checked.
when: Always.

name: The app's words of the take reused
what: The words the app heard as a take arrived in the editor (.prep/words.json, Whisper large-v3, its language detected) become the take's transcript when they are of this very file and in the language asked: nothing heard twice.
when: A take dropped in the Short video editor (the Whiteboard style); any run with a .prep/ of the same file.
why: OPTIMISATION: transcription never repeated (RELEASE-CHECKLIST § 0).
